script: add structural_merkle_hash for template identification
Contributed by Ziyang (as exfer-stack) upstream to ahuman-exfer/exfer, the Exfer chain itself.
This pull request is merged.
https://github.com/ahuman-exfer/exfer/pull/22

## Motivation

\`merkle_hash\` commits to the full program, including every \`Const(v)\` value. This is required for Merkleized-script spending security: two contracts that differ only in their embedded constants must hash differently, otherwise one could be substituted for the other at spend time.

That property makes \`merkle_hash\` unsuitable for a separate, common need: identifying the **template** a script was built from, independent of its specific parameter values.

Example use cases:

- A block explorer wanting to label outputs as \"Standard HTLC\" without enumerating every possible \`(sender, receiver, hashlock, timeout)\` tuple.
- An audit / attestation tool answering \"how many HTLCs of this kind has address X settled?\" — where the answer should aggregate across parameter values.
- A reputation graph keyed on contract type rather than instance.
- Anyone writing tooling that needs to ask \"what *kind* of contract is this?\" without caring about specific embedded constants.

## What this PR adds

A new function \`structural_merkle_hash(&Program) -> Hash256\` next to the existing \`merkle_hash\`. It uses the same recursion, except every \`Combinator::Const(_)\` is hashed without its value bytes — so two programs with identical combinator structure but different embedded constants produce the same root.

\`\`\`rust
/// Compute the **structural** Merkle hash of a program — the same
/// recursion as \`merkle_hash\`, except every \`Combinator::Const(v)\`
/// is hashed without its value bytes. Two programs with identical
/// combinator structure but different embedded constants produce the
/// same structural hash.
pub fn structural_merkle_hash(program: &Program) -> Hash256
\`\`\`

The docstring on the function explicitly calls out that this is **not** a script commitment and **must not** be used by consensus to authorise spending — the chain's existing per-output script commitment continues to use the raw script bytes, and \`merkle_hash\` continues to commit to the full program including its constants.

## Compatibility

- Purely additive. \`merkle_hash\` is unchanged byte-for-byte.
- No consensus / validation code path is touched. No on-chain or on-disk encoding changes.
- No new dependencies.
- The new function is re-exported from \`exfer::script\` alongside the existing one.

## Tests

Four unit tests in \`src/script/serialize.rs\`:

- \`same_template_different_constants_yield_same_structural_hash\` — two HTLCs with totally different params hash to the same structural root, while their \`merkle_hash\` differs.
- \`different_structures_yield_different_structural_hashes\` — HTLC vs sig-only program produce different structural roots.
- \`const_free_program_matches_merkle_hash\` — for programs containing no \`Const\` nodes, structural and regular hashes agree by construction.
- \`structural_hash_is_deterministic\` — same input → same output across repeated calls.
